continuation_cursor.last_completed_action: User asked whether current CPU/RSS excludes iptables and requested a local sandbox simulation. Existing WBD smoke run 32814277618 already used udp2raw -a, so it is not literally firewall-free: udp2raw may install the FakeTCP/RST handling rule. However the transport benchmark does not model OpenWrt-style routed FORWARD/NAT/port-forward work, and cpu_ms_total sums only WBD userspace process CPU so kernel netfilter/softirq cost is not fully represented. The current sandbox is root with CAP_NET_RAW but lacks CAP_NET_ADMIN, so it cannot create netns/veth or install real iptables rules. A local C UDP relay upper-bound microbenchmark was run instead: 100000 x 1200-byte echo transactions, five repeats. Direct median goodput ~1467.9 Mbps; one userspace relay median ~1200.2 Mbps, relay CPU ~710 ms for 200000 forwarded datagrams (~3.55 us/datagram) and RSS ~1412 KiB; two relays median ~403.3 Mbps, relay CPU ~2130 ms and RSS ~2832 KiB, with one unstable repeat. This demonstrates userspace port forwarding substantially overestimates kernel netfilter memory/CPU. To measure the real increment cleanly, scripts/bench_netfilter_overhead.py and tests/test_netfilter_bench_optional.py landed at ce7acafbc65b0c0aaa25190f573565d2f5a81feb. The probe uses client-router-server namespaces and compares plain routing, FORWARD+conntrack, and DNAT+MASQUERADE+FORWARD at a fixed iperf3 UDP offered load while recording throughput, loss, iperf CPU, global busy CPU, softirq deltas, conntrack count and relevant slab activity. PR #3 is temporarily titled [netfilter-bench] so this handoff commit triggers the opt-in test in the already-registered CI workflow.
